title: Utility difficulty and tenure sit beside a sparse child-care time-loss endpoint
source_unit: positive-weight SIPP person pair with utility condition and tenure at month t, followed by conditional child-care work-prevention and time-loss fields

observations.period: 2024 reference year; November-to-December; utility difficulty and owner/buyer

denominator.unit: eligible person pairs with valid conditional time-loss amount

observations.method: Conditional descriptive mean using WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Only four eligible pairs contribute; zero replicate dispersion does not imply precision or representativeness. ETIMELOST is conditional on EWORKMORE=1 and a valid time-loss response.
observations.subgroup: Reference-parent person pairs with utility-payment difficulty, owner/buyer tenure, reported child-care work prevention, and valid time-loss amount.
observations.counterinterpretation: Utility difficulty is not a dated bill or shutoff, and tenure groups differ in composition, schedules, care arrangements, and ability to avoid reported time loss.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; November-to-December; utility difficulty and renter

denominator.unit: eligible person pairs with valid conditional time-loss amount

observations.method: Conditional descriptive mean using WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Only three eligible pairs contribute. ETIMELOST is conditional on EWORKMORE=1 and a valid time-loss response, and the annual care measure is not a monthly December outcome.
observations.subgroup: Reference-parent person pairs with utility-payment difficulty, renter tenure, reported child-care work prevention, and valid time-loss amount.
observations.counterinterpretation: The estimate is too sparse for a renter-owner ranking; utility difficulty and tenure do not identify a causal pathway to time loss.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; November-to-December; no utility difficulty and owner/buyer

denominator.unit: eligible person pairs with valid conditional time-loss amount

observations.method: Conditional descriptive mean using WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison is within a selected EWORKMORE=1 universe; people without reported work prevention do not supply a comparable time-loss response.
observations.subgroup: Reference-parent person pairs without reported utility-payment difficulty, owner/buyer tenure, reported child-care work prevention, and valid time-loss amount.
observations.counterinterpretation: No-utility-difficulty status is not an absence of all material pressure, and the result does not establish that utility conditions change care or work time.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; November-to-December; no utility difficulty and renter

denominator.unit: eligible person pairs with valid conditional time-loss amount

observations.method: Conditional descriptive mean using WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison is within a selected EWORKMORE=1 universe; the annual care measure is not a monthly December outcome.
observations.subgroup: Reference-parent person pairs without reported utility-payment difficulty, renter tenure, reported child-care work prevention, and valid time-loss amount.
observations.counterinterpretation: The estimate describes selected respondents, not renter care burden or a utility effect; reporting scale and work/care arrangements may differ across cells.

related_sources.claim: Defines the utility/tenure-to-conditional-time-loss design and its 27-pair sparse boundary.
Provides the broader resource-endpoint time-loss comparison and conditional interpretation.
Official definitions and universes for utility, tenure, work-prevention, and time-loss fields.

reproduction_audit.result: The four conditional means reproduce the committed local utility-time-loss output.
reproduction_audit.interpretation: Reproduction confirms a sparse descriptive endpoint, not a causal utility, tenure, care, work, recovery, trust, or political-action estimate. Raw inputs remain outside the repository.

boundary: This is a 27-pair conditional timing screen. Utility difficulty is not a dated bill, shutoff, or assistance decision; ETIMELOST is conditional on reported work prevention and a valid fall-reference-year time-loss response. No no-prevention comparison, household prevalence, causal effect, downstream hardship, recovery, remedy, trust, political action, or exit is established.
